summaries.n-tokenized-assets: Coins whose metadata describes tokenized stocks or real-world assets (RWAs). @RobinhoodCrypto posted on 2026-10-08 that it is exploring a Stock Token linked to an actively managed ETF with T. Rowe Price DA ("if successful"), and on 2026-09-08 that Robinhood Stock Tokens had reached $150M in TVL on Robinhood Chain. Apps built around those tokens have coins of their own: Borro.Markets (BORRO; "Lend, borrow and short stock tokens"), HyperDex (HYDX; "Unified Marketplace for Tokenized Assets & RWAs"), Prism Assets (PRISM; "tokenising real-world assets with AI"), Longbow (BOW; borrow USDG against tokenized stocks and RWAs), Quanta Pools (QUANTA; liquidity across Stock Tokens and RWAs), Mintfolio (MINTFOLIO; baskets of stocks and ETFs) and TARTAGLIA (TATA; "ZK dark pool for tokenized stocks"). On Solana, Tokenize Everything (EVERYTHING; pool created 2026-10-07) describes tokenized RWAs as the biggest crypto meta of the last year and a half; one 2026-10-07 post by @RaOnChain called it a scam. None of the coins is shown to be issued by or affiliated with Robinhood, and their product descriptions are their own claims. Measured: eight coins across all their pools.

n-tokenized-assets.notice: @RobinhoodCrypto (2026-10-08) said it is exploring a Stock Token linked to an actively managed ETF with T. Rowe Price DA and, if successful, it would be the first of its kind; it posted on 2026-10-06 that Stock Tokens are built for a minted-trading-yielding flywheel and on 2026-09-08 that they reached $150M TVL on Robinhood Chain. Borro.Markets (2026-10-06) says it built Uniswap v4 hooks for stock tokens.
n-tokenized-assets.interpretation: Robinhood Chain stock tokens are an official product with a fresh announcement, and a group of apps around them now have coins (lending, credit, liquidity, basket and dark-pool projects). The coins are not shown to be issued by or affiliated with Robinhood, and product claims are the projects' own and not verified here. EVERYTHING is a Solana meme on the theme that one account called a scam; its volume has fallen sharply from launch day.
